prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 中文 · API 参数说明 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "参数" · longest unbreakable word 122px · one-line width 122px
  col 2: header "类型" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 49px
  col 3: header "必填" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 4: header "默认值" · longest unbreakable word 82px · one-line width 82px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 97px · one-line width 488px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated poor: The description starts beyond the viewport, and the default value created_at breaks across lines. Readers must scroll to understand each parameter. | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: Parameter names, types and default values remain intact, with relatively compact rows. The description column is outside the initial viewport, so reading the table requires horizontal scrolling. | another layout was rated poor: The 必填 header wraps, the description begins beyond the viewport, and the tall rows make comparisons harder. | another layout was rated bad: The whole table fits, but parameter names and default values split inside identifiers. The narrow description column also produces very tall, difficult-to-scan rows. | another layout was rated acceptable: The visible identifiers and values stay intact, but the description is offscreen and the rows are taller than in B. | another layout was rated poor: The visible identifiers stay intact, but descriptions are offscreen and the tall rows leave considerable blank space across the visible columns.
another layout was rated acceptable: 参数名和类型清楚且保持完整，但说明列在视口外，阅读每行含义需要横向滚动。截图未显示说明列，无法判断其排版。 | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: 可见的参数名和类型完整，行距也较紧凑；但说明列在视口外，截图未显示其宽度和换行。 | another layout was rated poor: 说明列几乎完全在视口外，默认值 created_at 也被拆成两行；右侧只露出一小部分说明文字。 | another layout was rated poor: 必填表头被拆成两行，说明列只露出一小部分，行高也很大；参数名和默认值倒是保持完整。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 可见的参数名和类型保持完整，但说明列在视口外，截图也未显示其排版；行高比 B 更大。 | another layout was rated poor: 所有列都在视口内，但参数名、默认值和说明中的代码词频繁断开，说明列过窄，导致表格很长且难以扫描。
